description: PyroChronos es una aplicación web enfocada en la armonización de datos satelitales históricos de incendios activos (MODIS y VIIRS de NASA FIRMS). El sistema unifica más de dos décadas de registros en una grilla espacial continua para visualizar en un solo calendario la estacionalidad de fuegos, detectar periodos anómalos y facilitar la respuesta de emergencias y científicos.
summary:
PyroChronos harmonizes NASA FIRMS active-fire detections from MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS S-NPP (since 2012) into a single, consistent fire calendar. Because the two sensors differ in resolution, overpass times and confidence scales, their raw hotspot counts cannot be compared directly. We normalize both into a common schema, project them onto a shared 0.01° grid, and count "fire cell-days" instead of raw points, then estimate a VIIRS/MODIS factor with uncertainty and agreement metrics.

The result is a web app (plus a Telegram bot) where a firefighting brigade can answer, in under a minute: when does my fire season start, is this year stronger than previous ones, and where should I look first. It shows a year × month/week heat calendar with anomalies, a map of hotspots, a season "traffic light" based on the zone's own history, and a printable executive report.

We tested it with real data for Peru (2000-2025). It is historical analysis and ~3-hour-latency detection that requires field confirmation; it is not a prediction system.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

PyroChronos turns two inconsistent satellite fire records into one trustworthy timeline. Brigades and emergency committees in regions with a marked dry season (starting with Peru and the Amazon) can see when fire season begins, whether the current month is above the zone's historical median, and where activity concentrates.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Download: MODIS and VIIRS S-NPP hotspot CSVs from NASA FIRMS.

2. Normalize: a common schema (date, lat, lon, source, confidence unified to 0/1/2, FRP, type).

3. Grid: a shared 0.01° grid; the main metric is "fire cell-days", which avoids double counting between sensors with different pixel sizes.

4. Harmonize: a VIIRS/MODIS factor over their overlap period, with uncertainty and concordance.

5. Anomalies: leave-one-out percentiles (±1 window) compare each period with the zone's own history.

6. Deliver: web dashboard (calendar, map with drawable zone, year vs. median chart with 25-75 percentile band, CSV downloads, season traffic light, printable PDF report) and a Telegram bot for alerts.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Brigades can plan staffing and prevention before the season starts, using a calendar that does not change depending on which sensor was used. The plain-language summaries are template-based, so every statement can be traced to data.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, pandas/Parquet, React + Vite + Tailwind + Leaflet, Telegram Bot API. 53 automated tests plus a UI smoke test. All thresholds are configurable in config.yaml. Code: https://github.com/JohanaQuispe/pyrochronos (MIT license).

CREATIVITY

Instead of another hotspot map, we focus on time: a harmonized calendar that tells a brigade when to be ready. We are explicit about limits: no real-time claims, no prediction, and every alert asks for field confirmation.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Sensor differences (resolution, overpass time, confidence scales), double counting, ~3 h latency of recent data, false positives (hence human validation), and data provenance (documented with dates and hashes).

CURRENT STATUS

Historical analysis, calendar, map, traffic light and reports are verified with real Peru data. Telegram alerts run in simulation mode, and near-real-time mode is implemented but requires a FIRMS key. These limits are documented in docs/verificado.md.
